title: What If You Had an Eagle's Eyes? You'd See an Ant From 10 Floors Up

scenes.text: What if you had an eagle's eyes? Reading wouldn't change. Everything else would.
Eagles see 20/5 or 20/4. What you can make out at five feet, they see from twenty. Four to five times farther than you.
From the roof of a ten-storey building you could watch an ant crawl on the pavement. A rabbit running three miles away would be visible.
Each eye would have two foveas, one for close work, one for distance, packed with a million cones per millimetre. Yours have about 200,000.
Your eyes would sit angled 30 degrees apart, fixed in their sockets, giving you a 340-degree view instead of 180.
And you'd see ultraviolet, including the glowing urine trails of mice. Eagle expert William Hodos puts it this way: we can't even guess what that looks like.

description:
What if you had an eagle's eyes? Eagles see at 20/5 or 20/4, four to five times farther than a person with normal vision, so you could spot an ant from the roof of a ten-storey building or a rabbit running about three miles away. Each eye would have two foveae packed with about a million cones per millimetre against roughly 200,000 in a human fovea, your eyes would sit angled 30 degrees from the midline for a 340-degree field of view, and you would see ultraviolet light, including the urine trails of small prey.
Bird vision expert William Hodos of the University of Maryland says colours would look more vivid than we can imagine. Reading a newspaper, however, would feel about the same.

first_comment: The catch: with that many cones and fewer rods, your night vision would get worse. Which animal sense would you borrow? Drop your own what-if below.
